BiblicalUsage: The night watch is the division of the night when the guard changes, and God moves in it. In the morning watch the LORD looks through the pillar of fire and of the cloud and troubles the host of Egypt, Gideon comes to the camp in the beginning of the middle watch, and Saul smites the Ammonites in the morning watch.
TheologicalSignificance: I believe the morning watch is God's hour: the Egyptians are troubled in it, Gideon strikes in it, and Saul wins in it. The night is divided into watches, and I hold that the God who keeps the last watch is the God who fights for His people while they sleep.
